ABSTRACT 
At present, the global energy supply is generally sufficient but the structure is tight. Supercapacitors have the 
characteristics of high power density, extremely fast charging and discharging, long cycle life, and wide operating 
temperature range. This article reviews t he research progress of the application of biomass-based materials in supercapa 
citor electrode materials, and elabo rately discusses the types of bio mass materials, their p reparation methods, th e 
structure and working principle of supercapacito rs, as well as th e performance of biomass-based materials as electrode 
materials. Biological-based materials can significantly enhance the performance of supercapacitors through various 
preparation methods. In  particu lar, biomass carb on materials, due to their high specific surface area and excellent 
conductivity, have become a research hotsp ot for electrode materials in supercapacitors.  This article provides a 
theoretical basis for future research to further optimize the preparation process of biomass-based materials and 
enhance their electrochemical performance, thereby promoting their development in practical applications. 
Keywords: Biomass; Electrode Material; Supercapacitor; Capacitive Performance; Research Progress. 
1. INTRODUCTION
With the steady rise in global energy consumption and the escalating severity of environmental challenges, advancing 
high-performance and sustainable energy storage technologies has emerged as a central focus of contemporary scientific 
research. [1] As an emerging energy storage technology, supercapacitors have attracted considerable interest owing to their 
outstanding power density, fast charge–discharge performance, and excellent cycling stability. They have promising 
applications in electric vehicles, portable electronic devices, and renewable energy systems. However, the energy density 
of supercapacitors is relatively low, which limits their application in certain scenarios with high energy demands. Therefore, 
improving the energy density and overall performance of supercapacitors through material selection and structural design 
has become the current research focus. 
In recent  years, biomass-based  electrode materials have gradually become a new research  direction in the  field of 
supercapacitor electrode materials due to  their wide sources, s trong renewability, environmental friendliness, as well as 
their unique structural and functional characteristics. Biological materials mainly come from animals and plants, 
microorganisms and their derivatives, as well as biological waste. Their main components are organic polymer substances 
composed of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. The biomass materials processed and prepared through physical, chemical or 
biological methods can not only effectively utilize renewable resources, but also significantly enhance the performance of 
supercapacitors through  various carbonization methods and composite material preparation methods. Sun et al. [2] 
synthesized a heteroatom-doped carbon material (CHPC‑X) with a three‑dimensionally interconnected network by 
employing biomass‑derived precursors such as chitosan and sodium lignosulfonate, where boric acid served as both a 
structural template and an auxiliary agent, and KOH was used as  the activating agent. Among them, the best-performing 
part has a high specific surface area of 2700.65 m2 g-1. In a three-electrode system using 6 M KOH as the electrolyte, the 
specific capacitance of CHPC-X at 1 A g-1 is 332 F g-1, and the energy density of the CHPC-X//CHPC-X symmetric 
electrode can reach 17.7 W h kg-1 (166.4 W k g-1). In addition, Rui Ding[3] reported a method for preparing three-
dimensional network porous carbon materials by using intermittent activation and freeze-drying pretreatment. Due to its 
high porosity, after 100 cycles at a charging and discharging c urrent density of 0.2 A g⁻¹, the specific capacity exceeded 
900 mA h g⁻¹, and after 500 cycles, the specific capacity exceeded 500 mA h g⁻¹, demonstrating excellent electrochemical 
performance.

materials. Firstly, it introduces the basic concepts, types and characteristics of biomass-based materials; Secondly, it

Abstract
This research investigates the use of machine learning (ML) to improve the performance of conducting polymer-based 
electrodes in supercapacitors, which leverage both electric double-layer capacitance (EDLC) and pseudocapacitive charac-
teristics. Six ML models—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Decision 
Tree (DT), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)—are evaluated for their ability 
to predict the specific capacitance of electrodes using an experimental dataset comprising Polyaniline (PANI), Polypyrrole 
(Ppy), and Polythiophene (PTh). Performance metrics included Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), 
and R-squared  (R2). Among the models, MLP demonstrates superior predictive accuracy, achieving the lowest MAE of 0.1452 
and MSE of 0.0373, along with the highest  R2 of 0.9622. In contrast, Decision Tree and SVM exhibited higher error values, 
with MAEs of 0.2107 and 0.2267 and  R2 values around 0.885. Although Random Forest and XGBoost achieved competitive 
 R2 values of 0.9399 and 0.9354, their errors are comparatively higher than MLP. These results highlight the effectiveness of 
advanced ML techniques in enhancing supercapacitor technology and indicate the potential of these models to predict and 
optimize conducting polymer-based electrode materials for improved performance.
Keywords Supercapacitors · Conducting Polymers · Machine Learning · Specific Capacitance · Polyaniline · Polypyrrole · 
Polythiophene · Multilayer Perceptron
1 Introduction
Supercapacitors, often referred to as electrochemical capaci-
tors or ultracapacitors, are devices used for storing energy. 
They can store a large amount of power, have a long lifes -
pan, and can charge and discharge quickly. These charac-
teristics render them appropriate for a wide range of uses 
such as portable electronic devices, electric cars, and renew-
able energy systems. The performance of supercapacitors 
is largely determined by the properties of the electrode 
materials used. Conducting polymers and their composites 
have emerged as promising electrode materials due to their 
high electrical conductivity, pseudocapacitive behavior, and 
ease of synthesis [1 ]. Pseudocapacitors, particularly those 
utilizing conducting polymers, have garnered significant 
attention recently because of their remarkable capacity 
for storing energy with extended periods of maintenance-
free durability, high cycle efficiency, and substantial power 
density. Pseudocapacitors are poised to narrow the current 
divide in energy storage between traditional capacitors and 
electrochemical batteries, offering a balance of energy and 
power density that is advantageous for various applications. 
Conducting polymer-based pseudocapacitors are promising 
due to their high specific capacitance, flexible structure, and 
high-speed charging and discharging capabilities (Fig.  1). 
These attributes make them suitable for use in industrial 
sectors and consumer electronics, including electric vehi-
cles, portable electronics, and backup power supplies [2 ].
However, a critical challenge remains in enhancing their 
energy density which continues to be a significant limiting 
factor preventing more widespread adoption. Addressing this 
issue is crucial for the advancement and integration of pseu-
docapacitors in broader energy storage applications. Pseu-
docapacitors utilize rapid and reversible redox processes

ABSTRACT
For supercapacitor electrodes, carbon is one of the most sought materials. Many 
synthetic strategies have been reported for carbon materials with a wide range 
of features in terms of surface area, porosity, the extent of the disorder, and 
the presence of various doping elements. Though there are many reports on the 
independent impact of these properties on supercapacitive outcomes of carbon 
materials, the collective effect of these features on the supercapacitive behavior 
is still not well understood. Therefore, it is imperative to explore new methods 
to predict the supercapacitive performance of carbon material without attempt-
ing experimentation. In this regard, this work reports on the comparative effi-
cacy of five machine-learning (ML) techniques for estimating the capacitance of 
carbon-based supercapacitors, including Linear Regression, Lasso Regression, 
XGBoost, Random Forest Regressor, and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). We 
gathered data from various research papers and articles to prepare the dataset, 
followed by Data Cleaning and Feature Selection to select the best parameters 
for training our Machine Learning model. Additionally, five factors were cho-
sen to determine their effects on capacitance: voltage window, specific surface 
area  (m2/g), pore size (nm),  ID/IG ratio, and extent of N-doping. Out of five ML 
approaches, XGBoost, Random Forest Regressor, and Artificial Neural Networks 
(ANN) produced respectable prediction results when tested against actual data. 
More significantly, this project demonstrates the promise of Machine-Learning 
in selecting suitable materials for energy storage applications.

because of different charge storage mechanisms oper-
ating in batteries and supercapacitors. While charge

Machine learning‑optimized hybrid graphene/
polymer electrodes for high‑performance 
and scalable supercapacitors
Maziyar Sabet1,* 
1 Chemical and Energy Engineering, Universiti Teknologi Brunei, Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei Darussalam
ABSTRACT
The demand for carbon-based materials with superior electrochemical properties 
continues to grow, particularly for scalable supercapacitor applications. In this 
study, we present a hybrid synthesis route for graphene electrodes that combines 
chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and microwave-assisted reduction, guided by 
machine learning (ML) optimization. A predictive neural network trained on over 
100 synthesis experiments enabled precise tuning of key parameters, resulting in 
high conductivity (~ 9.6 × 105 S  m−1). Raman analysis across ≥ 5 spots per sample 
showed hybrid graphene at ID/IG = 0.29 [mean ± SD to be reported], while the 
CVD control exhibited ID/IG ≈ 0.10 [mean ± SD]. These properties underpinned 
the electrodes’ high specific capacitance (up to 500 F  g−1), energy density (120 Wh 
 k g−1), and 95% retention over 10,000 cycles. The synthesized graphene was further 
hybridized with  MnO2,  RuO2, and conductive polymers (polyaniline, polypyr-
role), leading to enhanced specific capacitance, energy density, and power den-
sity (70 kW  kg−1), while maintaining long-term stability. Structural, thermal, and 
electrochemical evaluations confirmed the durability and high performance of 
the optimized electrodes. This work demonstrates a scalable and cost-effective 
graphene synthesis strategy for advanced energy storage, enabled by machine 
learning. The integration of data-driven optimization with roll-to-roll-compat-
ible processing provides a promising pathway toward industrial deployment 
of graphene-based supercapacitors in transportation, grid systems, and flexible 
electronics.

A machine learning approach to optimize

Abbas A. Abdullahi1, Ahmad Abbas Dalhatu2, Abdul‑Rahman Faisal Al‑Betar1, Syed Shaheen Shah3, 
Syed Masiur Rahman4,6, Tawfik A. Saleh1, and Md. Abdul Aziz4,5,* 
1 Chemistry Department, King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals, Dhahran 31261, Saudi Arabia

Sakyo‑ku, Kyoto 606‑8501, Japan

ABSTRACT
This study presents a machine learning (ML)-driven framework for optimizing 
the design of polyaniline (PANI)-based supercapacitors, a promising material 
for energy storage. The framework integrates experimental data and advanced 
optimization techniques to systematically investigate the effects of key fabrication 
parameters such as mesh size, deposition cycles, voltage window, and operating 
potential on performance metrics, including specific capacitance, energy density, 
and internal resistance (IR) drop. Two ML models, gradient boosting regressor 
(GBR) and random forest regressor (RFR), were trained on 145 experimental data-
sets, achieving high predictive accuracy  (R2 > 0.95). Bayesian optimization (BO) 
was used to identify the global optimum fabrication conditions, resulting in sig-
nificant reductions in mean absolute percentage errors 15% for energy density, 
20% for capacitance, and 7% for IR drop. Feature importance analysis, includ-
ing SHAP and partial dependence plots, revealed that mesh size and operating 
potential were the most influential parameters, aligning with electrochemical 
theories on ion transport and polymer growth. This integrated approach not 
only accelerates the design and optimization of PANI-based supercapacitors but 
also minimizes material waste and provides a scalable, interpretable pathway for 
ML-driven optimization in the development of high-performance, cost-effective 
energy storage devices.

ABSTRACT
Recent years have seen remarkable progress in the integration of Density Func-
tional Theory (DFT) calculations and Machine Learning (ML) techniques, par-
ticularly within the realm of materials science. This review delves into this bur-
geoning field, focusing on their application to MXenes, a significant family of 
two-dimensional (2D) materials comprising transition metal carbides, nitrides, 
or carbonitrides. MXenes have garnered attention for their remarkable proper-
ties and versatile applications, including catalysis, gas sensing, and energy stor-
age. We further investigate the integration of ML methodologies, utilizing vari-
ous algorithms to predict MXene properties with high accuracy and efficiency. 
Through a comprehensive literature analysis, we underscore the synergistic rela-

ABSTRACT
This paper aims to develop machine learning (ML) models to predict bio-based 
supercapacitor energy density from electrode physical and elemental composi-
tion, as well as potential window (PW), to accelerate materials discovery and 
reduce the resources and time required for experimental optimization. Extreme 
gradient boosting (XGB), random forest (RF), extremely randomized tree (ERT) 
and categorical boosting (CB) ML algorithms were employed to develop predic-
tive ML models. The training datasets for ML models are extracted from experi-
mental data from existing published articles on bio-based supercapacitors. XGB, 
RF, ERT and RF models’ performance was evaluated with coefficient of deter-
mination (R2), root-mean-square error (RMSE), mean absolute percentage error 
(MAPE) and mean absolute error (MAE). Among the models, XGB had the best 
performance with R2 value of 0.885, followed by CB, RF and ERT at 0.841, 0.781 
and 0.637, respectively, when tested with new experimental data. With testing 
data, XGB recorded the lowest MAE of 4.81 Wh/kg, ERT, CB and RF recorded 
MAE of 9.23 Wh/kg, 6.51 Wh/kg and 8.14 Wh/kg, respectively. Shapley additive 
explanations (SHAP) analysis indicated that PW exhibited the highest impact 
in all models used to predict energy density as compared to other independent 
variables, such as specific surface area (SSA), intensity ratio (IR) and average 
pore size (PS), emphasizing its critical influence in developing predictive models 
and enhancing supercapacitor energy density. The impact of PW in predicting 
energy density of bio-based supercapacitors can be attributed to its quadratic 
relationship with energy density. Consequently, the models accurately pre-
dict bio-based supercapacitor energy density, demonstrating the role of PW in 
designing and optimizing bio-based materials for the development of sustainable 
supercapacitors.

ABSTRACT
Carbon-based electrode materials are widely recognized for their outstanding 
electrical conductivity, large specific surface area, and robust chemical stabil-
ity, thereby rendering them highly suitable for electric double-layer capacitors 
(EDLCs) that rely on electrostatic charge storage. Among these materials, bio-
mass-derived activated carbon (AC)—especially from agroforestry waste—has 
gained prominence as a potential candidate due to its cost-effectiveness, abundant 
availability, and simple synthesis processes. Numerous experimental investiga-
tions have explored the synthesis of AC from diverse biomass sources. Also, the 
research is now increasingly shifting toward predictive modeling to understand 
and optimize AC properties for supercapacitor applications. Recent efforts focus 
on forecasting key performance metrics such as yield, heteroatom content, and 
specific capacitance based on structural and compositional parameters, including 
pore architecture, chemical constituents, graphitization level, testing conditions, 
and electrolyte choice. This review presents a detailed analysis of AC fabrication 
techniques, the influence of processing variables on material performance, and 
the growing role of machine learning (ML) in predicting electrochemical behav-
ior. Particular emphasis is placed on linking synthesis conditions with structural 
characteristics and their impact on specific capacitance.

Abstract
Supercapacitors (SCs) are promising energy-storage systems whose efficiency largely depends on electrode composition 
and design. Utilizing carbon waste is vital for advancing sustainable technologies due to its high storage capacity, low cost, 
wide availability and eco-friendly nature. Biomass-derived carbon materials, with their high surface area, conductivity 
and environmental benefits, have emerged as strong candidates for next-generation SC electrodes. This review presents a 
systematic analysis of recent strategies for converting biomass waste into high-performance electrode materials for SCs. 
In addition, this summarizes an innovative thematic area where activated carbon is derived from novel sources like peanut 
shells, jujube shells, tea and coffee waste, hazelnuts, leather waste, paper waste etc. In addition, it encompasses the prepa -
ration of carbon-based products and strategies for enhancing porous structures by activation. Incorporating these materi -
als in SCs offers the dual benefit of enhancing energy storage performance while contributing to waste management and 
resource recycling. Importantly, this review introduces the novel concept of electrochemical double-layer compression due 
to solvated radicals, which modifies classical Helmholtz theory which has no prior literature. We further discuss the role of 
sequential chemical and physical activation in tuning porosity and ion transport with unique design proposal of sequential 
activation. Furthermore, future research directions are highlighted, zeroing in on promoting the scalability, electrochemi -
cal double-layer capacitor performance, and commercial credibility of such electrodes with the effects of impurities and 
quality control. This approach contributes to the development of low-cost, sustainable and scalable energy storage systems.

seventh of the data used by existing models to achieve the same performance.

Hybrid electric vehicles and portable electronic systems use supercapacitors for energy storage owing 
to their fast charging/discharging rates, long life cycle, and low maintenance. Specific capacitance 
is regarded as one of the most important performance-related characteristics of a supercapacitor’s 
electrode. In the current study, Machine Learning (ML) algorithms were used to determine the impact 
of various physicochemical properties of carbon-based materials on the capacitive performance of 
electric double-layer capacitors. Published experimental datasets from 147 references (4899 data 
entries) were extracted and then used to train and test the ML models, to determine the relative 
importance of electrode material features on specific capacitance. These features include current 
density, pore volume, pore size, presence of defects, potential window, specific surface area, oxygen, 
and nitrogen content of the carbon-based electrode material. Additionally, categorical variables 
as the testing method, electrolyte, and carbon structure of the electrodes are considered as well. 
Among five applied regression models, an extreme gradient boosting model was found to best 
correlate those features with the capacitive performance, highlighting that the specific surface area, 
the presence of nitrogen doping, and the potential window are the most significant descriptors for 
the specific capacitance. These findings are summarized in a modular and open-source application 
for estimating the capacitance of supercapacitors given, as only inputs, the features of their carbon-
based electrodes, the electrolyte and testing method. In perspective, this work introduces a new wide 
dataset of carbon electrodes for supercapacitors extracted from the experimental literature, also 
giving an instance of how electrochemical technology can benefit from ML models.
Electrochemical capacitors (supercapacitors) are electrochemical devices that are extensively used for energy stor-
age due to promising characteristics such as high-power density, electrochemical stability, fast charge/discharge 
rates, safe operation mode, high power density, and long cycle  life1–3. These characteristics enable their use in a 
broad range of energy storage applications, e.g., for hybrid electric vehicles, portable electronics, and memory 
backup  systems4–6. Other than energy storage, there are some further interesting applications of supercapaci-
tors such as heat-to-current conversion of low-grade thermal  energy7 and renewable energy extraction using 
a supercapacitor from water  solutions8. Supercapacitors have been primarily classified into two types based on 
their charge storage mechanism: (i) electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), which store electrical charge via 
ion adsorption at the electrode surface, and (ii) pseudo-capacitors, which store charges via reversible Faradaic

Abstract
This review examines the potential of supercapacitors (SCs) in simulating biological signals, with a particular focus 
on neural signaling applications. Owing to their rapid charge–discharge kinetics and high power density, SCs exhibit 
functional parallels with neuronal response mechanisms, positioning them as promising candidates for bioinspired elec -
trochemical devices. The paper begins by outlining the fundamental principles, material architectures, and performance 
characteristics of SCs. Subsequently, it establishes the theoretical framework for biological signal simulation, encom -
passing neural signal propagation mechanisms and the properties of bioelectrical signals. The core discussion centers 
on supercapacitor-based neural signal simulation, addressing the similarities in dynamic behavior with neuronal activity, 
supported by experimental findings and computational modeling. Current technological limitations, including material 
optimization, structural design, and biocompatibility challenges, are critically analyzed alongside potential solutions. The 
review concludes by highlighting emerging applications in neural interfaces and biomedical devices, while identifying key 
research directions for future investigation. This synthesis highlights the distinct advantages of SCs in bioelectronic signal 
emulation and underscores the need for continued exploration in this interdisciplinary field.

1 Introduction
Electricity has emerged as the principal currency of energy exchange in the modern 
world. The recent increase in the acceptance of electrically operated automobiles such 
as e-bicycles, e-mopeds, electric cars, hybrid buses, and e-rickshaws has amplified the 
demand and dependency on electrical power [ 1– 5]. The global rise in living standards 
can be largely accredited to increasing reliance on electrical power. The development of 
various electrochemical energy storage devices-such as conventional capacitors, super -
capacitors, batteries, and fuel cells has been crucial in addressing energy management 
Discover Electronics
Abstract
The design architecture of electrode materials plays a pivotal role in shaping the 
electrochemical performance of supercapacitor. The dimensionality of electrode 
material proposes trade-off between specific surface area, pore architecture, 
mechanical strength and flexibility. This review undertakes a comprehensive 
classification of electrode materials into zero-dimensional, one-dimensional, two-
dimensional, and three-dimensional architectures, further correlating their structural 
characteristics with surface area, electrical conductivity, and ion transport dynamics. 
Various classes of materials, including carbon-based nanostructures, transition metal 
oxides, transition metal dichalcogenides, MXenes, and metal–organic frameworks, 
are analysed with respect to morphology-dependent performance characteristics. 
The design of heterostructures and multi-dimensional electrodes, as well as various 
synthesis methods, and the crucial elements of sustainability and scalability, are also 
taken into account. Furthermore, viewpoints for future avenues that pave the way 
for the development of supercapacitors are presented. Overall, this review aims to 
bridge the understanding between dimensional architecture, synthesis approach 
and performance, offering acuity in rational material design strategies for sustainable, 
high-performance supercapacitor systems.

Abstract
This complete investigation presents a combined experimental and computational 
Approach to emergent high-performance nickel cobalt sulfide (NiCo 2S4) 
nanostructures for Supercapacitor applications. NiCo 2S4 samples were synthesised 
via a two-step solvothermal Method at temperatures of 120–180 °C (designated 
NCS1-NCS4) and scientifically characterised using XRD, BET, SEM, XPS and FTIR. 
The optimised NCS4 electrode exhibited a notable specific capacitance of 920.04 
Fg− 1 from cyclic voltammetry and 375 Fg − 1 from galvanostatic Charge-discharge 
measurements. DFT calculations revealed that the (111) surface has the lowest 
surface energy (0.85 Jm − 2) and the highest electrochemical activity, while nickel 
vacancies have the lowest formation energy (1.8 eV) under Ni-poor conditions. ML 
models achieved R 2 = 0.97 in predicting capacitance, with synthesis temperature 
identified as the most critical parameter (importance: 0.28). A Comparative analysis 
of simulated and experimental results showed excellent agreement (average 
deviation < 5%). The symmetric supercapacitor device achieved an exceptional 
specific capacitance of 1234.89 Fg − 1, an energy density of 42.9 Whkg − 1, a power 
density of 735 Wkg − 1, and 82.82% capacitance retention after 5000 cycles. Pre-
fabrication analysis indicated optimal mass loading of 1.5 mg cm − 2 and electrode 
thickness of 200 nm for device development. This integrated methodology provides 
a comprehensive framework for the rational design of transition metal sulfide 
electrodes, with applications in electric automobiles, portable semiconductor 
technology, renewable energy storage, and industrial power systems.

Spark Plasma Sintered Binder-Free Carbon Electrodes for 
Decoupled Water Electrolysis
Mārtiņš Vanags1, Mairis Iesalnieks1, Toms Valdemārs Eiduks1, Artūrs Plūdons1, Krišjānis 
Šmits2,3, Reinis Drunka1, Ints Šteins1, Andris Šutka1*

Valdena 3/7, Riga, LV1010, Latvia

Valdena Str. 3, Riga, LV-1048 Latvia
3Institute of Biomaterials and Bioengineering, Faculty of Natural Sciences and Technology, 
Riga Technical University, P. Valdena Str. 3, Riga, LV-1048 Latvia
Abstract
Water electrolysis is the dominant approach for producing green hydrogen from renewable 
energy, providing an alternative to fossil fuels. Conventional water electrolysis faces many 
problems due to the intermittent nature of renewable power and the need for a membrane to 
avoid the formation of an explosive gas mixture. To avoid the use of a membrane, the 
decoupled water electrolysis approach has been introduced, where one catalyst electrode is 
replaced by a solid redox mediator. So far, redox mediators for decoupled electrolysis have 
been prepared using fluoropolymer binders, which pose a serious environmental burden and 
are facing a ban. This is a limiting factor for further implementation of emerging decoupled 
water electrolysis technology. In this work, we report a binder-free charcoal electrode for use 
as a redox mediator electrode in acid and alkaline decoupled water electrolysis. The binder-
free redox mediator electrodes were prepared by a solvent-free spark plasma sintering. The 
sintering temperature was optimised to obtain a volumetric redox mediator with a high specific 
capacitance of 175 F g-1 and a specific charge capacity of 41 mAh g-1 at a current density of 50 
mA g-1. The observed values are higher than reported in the literature for volumetric carbon-
based supercapacitor materials. 
Keywords: Spark plasma sintering, decoupled electrolysis, activated charcoal, double-layer 
capacitor.
Introduction
The energy sector is currently undergoing a transformation from fossil to renewable energy 
sources (solar, wind, hydropower, tidal, etc.) [1]. Renewable energy is inexhaustible, and it 
does not pollute the environment. However, they are characterised by intermittency. Energy 
consumers require stability, availability, and energy security; therefore, there must be a stable, 
efficient, and secure connection between the renewable energy production plant and consumers. 
One of the most promising is “green hydrogen”.

Abstract
Cork, a porous biopolymer, is composed of hollow prismatic cells with thin walls 
arranged in a compact honeycomb-like structure, making it a promising material 
for adsorption applications. In this study, cork-derived activated carbon (CAC) 
was synthesized through pyrolysis followed by chemical activation using solid 
potassium hydroxide, with the aim of producing an efficient adsorbent for the 
removal of industrial dyes. The structure, morphology, and functional groups of the 
CAC were characterized using Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis, 
scanning electron microscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, Fourier transform 
infrared spectroscopy, and X-ray diffraction. BET surface area analysis revealed a 
high specific surface area of 1,793 m 2/g, favoring strong adsorption capacity. Batch 
and fixed-bed column experiments were conducted to evaluate the adsorption 
performance toward two representative dyes: Methylene blue (MB) and reactive red 
(RR). The pseudo-second-order kinetic model accurately described the adsorption 
behavior, while the Langmuir isotherm model indicated monolayer adsorption for 
MB, and the Freundlich model better fitted the heterogeneous adsorption of RR. The 
maximum adsorption capacities (q m) were 250 mg/g and 105 mg/g for MB and RR, 
respectively. Overall, the results demonstrate that the produced CAC exhibits high 
adsorption efficiency and holds significant potential for application in industrial 
effluent remediation and the treatment of water contaminated with persistent dye 
compounds.

Coal possesses a dense, cross-linked structure and strong π - π stacking interactions that hinder activator pene -
tration and cause excessive graphitization, which limits its application in zinc-ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs). 
Herein, we propose a synergistic deep eutectic solvent (DES) swelling and in-situ air carbonization strategy to 
fabricate defect-rich, heteroatom-doped porous carbon from raw coal. Utilizing the ZnCl

to 31.45% to facilitate deep activator penetration. During the subsequent air carbonization, the DES functions as 
a condensed-phase flame retardant to prevent over-burning, alongside serving as an in-situ activator and P 
dopant. The in-situ formation of thermally stable C-O-C bridge bonds introduces spatial steric hindrance that is 
proposed to promote a local hybridization shift from sp

carbon. This effectively inhibits the tight 
stacking of aromatic sheets and suppresses excessive graphitization. The optimized carbon is characterized by a

1. Introduction
Benefiting from their high safety, low cost, and fast charge transport 
kinetics, zinc-ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs) have attracted extensive 
research attention as potential energy storage candidates [ 1 ]. Due to 
their excellent electrical conductivity, tunable pore structures, and su -
perior electrochemical stability, porous carbons are widely utilized as 
cathode materials in ZIHCs [ 2 ]. Because the cathode crucially dictates 
the capacity and rate performance of ZIHCs, rationally designing porous 
carbon cathodes featuring both hierarchical porous channels and a 
highly active interface is important [ 3 ].
Coal serves as a cost-effective and carbon-rich precursor that con -
tains a 3D network. In this network, aliphatic chains and ether linkages 
connect polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and strong π - π 
stacking interactions also exist [ 4 ]. While such a highly aromatic 
structure endows coal-derived carbons with outstanding intrinsic con -
ductivity and structural stability, the tightly cross-linked matrix and 
potent intermolecular forces severely impede the diffusion of activators 
[ 5 ]. Consequently, the derived carbon materials often suffer from 
inhomogeneous pore evolution and constrained specific surface areas. 
Moreover, high-temperature carbonization in an inert atmosphere cau -
ses intense condensation and aromatization in PAH-rich coal [ 6 ]. This 
process preferentially produces highly graphitized carbons that lack 
structural defects and reactive sites. This highly ordered lattice config -
uration fails to offer adequate Faradaic charge compensation, thus 
severely limiting the overall electrochemical performance [ 7 ].

ABSTRACT
Harvesting the dispersed, low‐grade energy stored in atmospheric moisture has emerged as an attractive route toward 
distributed and sustainable power generation. Moisture‐induced electricity generation (MEG) converts chemical potential 
changes associated with water sorption, ion dissociation, selective ion transport, and interfacial charge transfer into electricity 
without requiring light, wind, or a liquid water supply. Natural biomass is a promising material platform because its polar and 
ionizable groups and hierarchical pore channels support moisture uptake, carrier generation, and directional ion transport. 
However, a single biomass material is unlikely to simultaneously provide high ionic conductivity, a persistent gradient, efficient 
charge collection, and wet‐state stability. This minireview presents a synergistic design framework across molecular, structural, 
and device levels. Biomass chemistry regulates carrier generation and ion selectivity, hierarchical structures maintain water 
activity and ion concentration gradients, and device integration coordinates ionic transport, charge collection, and structural 
stability. We first outline the fundamental mechanism of biomass‐based MEG and then compare cellulose, sodium alginate, 
lignin, proteins, chitosan, and microbial materials in terms of their properties, functions, limitations, and suitable application 
scenarios. Performance optimization strategies are further summarized as ionic regulation, gradient construction, and composite 
integration. Finally, we discuss the main challenges of conversion efficiency, operating lifetime, wet‐state durability, and 
biomass variability, together with future directions for practical and sustainable moisture energy harvesting.

Introduction
Rising global energy demand and the pursuit of carbon 
neutrality have intensified the search for clean and sustainable 
energy solutions. In this context, technologies capable of har -
vesting dispersed, low‐grade energy from ambient environments 
are emerging as a promising complementary pathway [ 1, 2 ]. The 
atmosphere, nearly ubiquitous yet long underexploited, repre -
sents one such reservoir, containing approximately 12,900 km
3 
of water vapor at any given time, with about 495,000 km
3 
of 
water circulating through the atmosphere each year via the hy -
drological cycle [ 3 ]. The adsorption and desorption of water 
molecules at material surfaces are accompanied by pronounced 
changes in chemical potential; if these can be directed into an 
electrical signal, energy can be harvested continuously in the 
absence of light, wind, or a liquid‐water supply. Building on this 
idea, moisture‐induced electricity generation (MEG) has 
advanced rapidly in recent years [ 4, 5 ]. For example, protein 
nanowires derived from Geobacter sustain self‐maintained po -
wer output under ambient humidity [ 6 ], adsorption–evaporation 
synergistic systems extend the continuous output of a single 
cycle to several hundred hours [ 7 ], and emerging platforms such 
as supramolecular hydrogels push the current to the milliampere 
level [ 8, 9 ], moving the technology from a concept toward 
practical use [ 5, 10 ].

ABSTRACT: As urgent demands increase in energy-grid systems, supercapacitors have been
further documented as highly promising energy-storage technologies across a range of
applications owing to their high-power density, rapid charge−discharge capabilities, and
prolonged endurance life. Porous carbon-based materials, particularly those derived from
metal−organic frameworks (MOFs), are prominent candidates for supercapacitor electrode
materials owing to their customizable inner-pore structures and superior electrochemical
properties. In this work, we systematically manipulate the carbonization temperature (700−900
°C) of Al-NDC-MOF to tailor the hierarchical pore structure, defect density, and surface
chemistry of the resulting porous carbons (AC-Al-NDC-x), aiming to unravel the structure−
performance−device correlations required for stable dual-ion storage. Systematic character-
ization reveals that carbonization temperature plays a crucial role in regulating pore structure
hierarchy, defect density, and surface functional groups. As a result, the optimized sample (AC-
Al-NDC-800) exhibits balanced electrochemical performance, enabling its application as both
positive and negative electrodes in symmetric and asymmetric two-electrode devices. This behavior is attributed to the synergistic
effect of micropores for charge storage, mesopores for ion transport, and appropriate surface functionalities for interfacial stability.
Although the achieved energy density and cycling stability are comparable to previously reported porous carbon systems, this work
highlights a rational design strategy for balancing pore structure and surface chemistry to achieve stable dual-ion storage under
practical two-electrode conditions.

1. INTRODUCTION
As advancements in electrochemical energy storage technology
continue, supercapacitors (SCs) have demonstrated distinct
advantages in various applications owing to their high-power
density, rapid charge−discharge capabilities,
1,2
and exceptional
cycling stability.
3,4
They have become indispensable compo-
nents in sectors such as industry,
5,6
energy,
7−9
and trans-
portation.
10,11
However, their relatively low energy density
presents a significant challenge for widespread adoption. This
limitation is primarily determined by the energy storage
mechanism, structural stability, and efficiency of the interfacial
reactions of the electrode materials within the different
operating potential windows.
Porous carbon-based materials, recognized for their high
specific surface area, customizable inner-porous net structure,
and excellent electrical conductivity, are regarded as prime
candidates for active SC electrode materials.
12,13
Among these,
carbon-based materials derived from metal−organic frame-
works (MOFs) have emerged as a focal point in contemporary
research owing to their significant advantages, such as a
designable and tunable precursor structure and a controllable
thermal conversion process.
14−17
By meticulously adjusting
process parameters, such as carbonization temperature and
activation intensity, it is possible to synergistically optimize the
key properties of MOF-derived carbon materials, such as the
specific surface area, pore structure distribution, defect density,
and surface chemical composition, thereby enhancing their
electrochemical energy-storage performance.

Numerous
studies have demonstrated that these materials can achieve a
high specific capacitance in three-electrode systems and exhibit
good rate capability in two-electrode devices.

aromatic ligands represent a promising yet relatively underex-
plored category of precursors for porous carbon electrodes,
although several recent studies have begun to explore Al-MOF-

Keywords: activated carbon, birch wood, NaOH activation, pore structure, supercapacitors, 
aqueous electrolyte
The valorization of biomass residues into advanced carbon materials offers a promising route 
toward more sustainable supercapacitor technologies. Birchwood was evaluated as a 
sustainable precursor for activated carbon electrodes in aqueous supercapacitors. Carbon was 
produced via carbonization, grinding, and activated at 700 or 800 °C using varying quantities 
of NaOH. Structural characterization (N₂ sorption at 77 K, XRD, Raman, SEM, elemental 
analysis, XPS) indicated specific surface areas up to 2401 m 2 g-1 and a temperature‑dependent 
pore architecture: predominantly microporous at 700 °C and mixed micro/mesoporous at 
800 °C. Electrochemical performance was assessed in symmetric CR2032 coin cells with a 
phosphate buffer electrolyte, using CV and GCD. The highest specific capacitance reached 
247 F g-1, exceeding that of commercial carbon Kuraray YP-80F by up to 115% under given 
test conditions. Although more pronounced graphitic structures develop after treatment at 
800 °C and may enhance conductivity, they also coincide with reduced surface area and 
consequently do not improve capacitance. Samples activated at 700 °C generally delivered 
superior capacitance and competitive rate capability, likely due to enhanced microporosity 
which increases the accessible surface area for electric double‑layer formation. These results 
suggest birchwood is a viable high‑value feedstock for carbon-based supercapacitor electrodes.

ABSTRACT: Metals in spent all-solid-state sodium-ion batteries
(ASIBs) pose severe environmental pollution, resource depletion,
and health risks. However, selective and sustainable recovery of
these metals from ASIBs remains highly challenging. Herein, we
introduce a coordination-solvation dual-regulation (CSDR) mech-
anism that enables, for the first time, the recovery of both the
cathode and solid electrolyte from ASIBs with exceptional
selectivity and high sustainability. Guided by this CSDR
mechanism, amino acid−based green solvents are employed with
a dual function: abundant functional groups provide coordination
sites for target metal ions while facilitating favorable solvation
interactions, collectively enabling metal leaching. Mechanistically,
the superior Na over Zr selectivity originates from differential
binding energetics, Na
+

4+

fractionation and delignification with industrial potential

ABSTRACT
Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) represent a new generation of environmentally friendly solvents that show great 
promise for sustainable lignocellulosic biomass separation. The article presents an original assessment of DES 
formulations through advanced computational modeling and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, which 
reveal essential mechanistic details that previous reviews have not fully explored. This work reviews MD sim -
ulations, DFT, and ML methods to study detailed hydrogen-bonding systems and proton-catalytic and ionic in -
teractions between DESs and biomass components, which leads to their high selectivity for lignin and 
hemicellulose extraction. The review establishes a fundamental understanding of DESs by studying their 
chemical makeup and physical characteristics, and experimental results when processing different biomass 
materials. The review combines molecular-level findings with process optimization methods, economic assess -
ments, and sustainability impact evaluations. The review establishes a complete understanding by connecting 
atomic-scale interactions to industrial-scale applications through computational modeling, which enables the 
creation of optimized DES-based biorefinery systems.
1. Introduction
Growing global demand for energy and materials, coupled with 
climate concerns and fossil fuel depletion, drives the search for renew -
able alternatives. Lignocellulosic biomass and microalgae offer prom -
ising, sustainable raw materials used in producing energy sources, 
chemical products, and industrial compounds, lessening the usage of oil, 
along with limiting environmental outcomes.
The environmental viability and process effectiveness of the different 
methods of breaking down biomass face multiple essential barriers in 
their conventional approaches. The NaOH/urea pretreatment from 
agricultural residues of rice straw enhances plant-based polysaccharides 
like cellulose and hemicellulose, achieving high yields but producing 
excessive salts, which need costly removal procedures ( Dong et al., 
2018 ). Application of organic liquids for hemicellulose and lignin 
removal from poplar through organic acid/solvent blends proves effec -
tive yet remains impractical because it requires substantial solvent 
volumes and produces harmful compounds ( Yang et al., 2020 ). The 
conventional methods experience three major drawbacks, which include 
equipment corrosion, high operational costs, and complex chemical 
recovery procedures, thus limiting their suitability for large-scale 
sustainable biomass processing ( Rastogi and Shrivastava, 2017 ). 
Organic solvents used in conventional processes face multiple draw -
backs, including their volatile nature and corrosive effects on equipment 
and toxic properties, which prevent their use in biomass processing 
( Hong et al., 2020 ). Specific advantages associated with ionic liquids 
(ILs) make them attractive for lignocellulosic biorefinery applications 
because they are non-flammable, have low vapor pressure, and lack 
volatility ( Wang et al., 2017 ). The extensive deployment of ILs is limited 
by their expensive production costs and challenging preparation 
methods.
Deep eutectic solvents (DES) present an environmentally friendly 
solution to traditional biomass pretreatment procedures through their 
ability to overcome major challenges, including high energy re -
quirements and corrosive or expensive chemical usage. The pretreat -
ment process with DES produces better glucose yields and maintains 
stable cellulase enzymes while decreasing both energy requirements and 
environmental effects ( Liu et al., 2019; Tan et al., 2018; Sai and Lee, 
2019 ). The DES method operates without requiring severe processing 
conditions or expensive solvents that traditional methods need. The 
fractionation of complex biomass microalgae through biomass process -
ing using DES composed of lactic acid (LA) and choline chloride (ChCl)

 Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan elektroda karbon monolitik bebas perekat 
berbasis limbah daun lobak yang berasal dari residu sayuran pasar sebagai prekursor 
biomassa untuk aplikasi superkapasitor dengan fokus pada peningkatan kinerja 
kapasitansi volumetrik. Elektroda karbon disintesis melalui tahapan pra -karbonisasi 
biomassa, pencetakan bertekanan tinggi untuk membentuk struktur monolitik, dan 
pirolisis pada suhu 800 °C dalam atmosfer inert tanpa penggunaan bahan pengikat. Dua 
jenis sampel dikembangkan, yaitu karbon tanpa perlakuan (DLK) dan karbon dengan 
impregnasi awal menggunakan larutan H₃PO₄ sebelum proses karbonisasi (DLK -P). 
Karakterisasi dilakukan terhadap perubahan densitas m aterial, morfologi permukaan, 
serta komposisi unsur untuk memahami pengaruh perlakuan kimia terhadap struktur 
karbon yang terbentuk. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa impregnasi awal H₃PO₄ 
mampu menghasilkan struktur karbon yang lebih homogen dan meningkatk an 
konduktivitas material tanpa mengurangi stabilitas mekanik elektroda monolitik. 
Evaluasi elektrokimia menggunakan metode voltametri siklik menunjukkan bahwa 
elektroda DLK -P memiliki respons kapasitif yang lebih baik dibandingkan elektroda 
tanpa perlakua n. Elektroda DLK -P menghasilkan kapasitansi volumetrik sebesar 109 
F/cm3, meningkat signifikan dibandingkan elektroda DLK yang hanya mencapai 53,4 
F/cm³. Nilai ini menunjukkan potensi kompetitif dibandingkan beberapa elektroda 
karbon berbasis biomassa yang telah dilaporkan sebelumnya. Hasil penelitian ini 
menunjukkan bahwa lim bah daun lobak berpotensi dimanfaatkan sebagai sumber 
karbon berkelanjutan untuk superkapasitor.

  ABSTRACT 
 This study aims to develop binder -free monolithic carbon electrodes derived from radish 
leaf waste, originating from vegetable market residues, as a biomass precursor for 
supercapacitor applications with a focus on enhancing volumetric capacitance 
performance. The carbon electrodes were synthesized through a sequence of biomass pre-
carbonization, high-pressure compaction to form a monolithic structure, and pyrolysis at 
800 °C under an inert atmosphere without the use of binders. Two types of samples were 
prepared: untreated carbon (DLK) and carbon with prior impregnation using an H₃PO₄ 
solution before the carbonization process (DLK -P). Characterization was conducted to 
examine changes in material density, surface morphology, and elemental composition in 
order to understand the influence of chemical treatment on the resulting carbon 
structure. The results indicate that H₃PO₄ pre -impregnation produces a more 
homogeneous carbon structure and enhances the electrical conductivity of the material 
without compromisi ng the mechanical stability of the monolithic electrode. 
Electrochemical evaluation using cyclic voltammetry shows that the DLK -P electrode 
exhibits a superior capacitive response compared to the untreated electrode. The DLK -P 
electrode delivers a volumetric capacitance of 109 F/cm3, significantly higher than the DLK 
electrode, which only reaches 53.4 F/cm3. These results demonstrate that radish leaf waste 
has strong potential as a sustainable carbon source for supercapacitor electrodes. 
Keywords:   organic waste, solid carbon, electrode, energy storage, supercapacitor

ABSTRACT
In this study, a novel eco-friendly electrode material was developed by utilizing the renewable biopolymer 
chitosan as the primary framework, reinforced with iron ions and silica nanoparticles (Fe-doped chitosan@SiO ₂ ). 
Chitosan, derived from natural biomass, offers abundant amino and hydroxyl functional groups that facilitate 
strong coordination with iron species and uniform anchoring of silica, leading to a robust porous network with 
enriched electroactive sites. Comprehensive physicochemical analyses, including SEM, TEM, XRD, FTIR, BET, 
and XPS, confirmed the successful incorporation and homogeneous dispersion of Fe and SiO ₂ within the chitosan 
matrix, resulting in a higher surface area and improved electrical conductivity. Electrochemical performance was 
systematically investigated using cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge – discharge, and electrochemical 
impedance spectroscopy in different aqueous electrolytes (NaOH, Na ₂ SO ₄ , and H ₂ SO ₄ ). The Fe-doped chito -
san@SiO ₂ electrode exhibited an outstanding specific capacitance of 404 F g

at a current density of 0.2 A g
� 1 
in 
acidic medium, significantly surpassing that of pristine chitosan. Moreover, it demonstrated excellent cyclic 
stability, maintaining 87.6 % of its initial capacitance after 5000 charge – discharge cycles. The incorporation of 
Fe notably reduced charge-transfer resistance, as evidenced by EIS, while Ragone plot analysis confirmed a well- 
balanced energy and power density. These findings highlight the promising potential of biomass-derived chitosan 
as a sustainable platform for the design of high-performance pseudocapacitive materials.

The rapid growth of portable electronics, electric vehicles, and 
renewable energy systems has intensified the search for advanced en -

promising candidates to fill this demand due to their excellent charge- 
discharge rates and superior durability compared to batteries. Howev -
er, a critical limitation lies in developing electrode materials that ach -
ieve both high energy and power densities while maintaining stability 
over prolonged cycles [ 4 , 5 ]. Carbon-based materials have dominated 
supercapacitor electrode research owing to their high electrical con -

pristine carbon materials frequently suffer from relatively low capaci -
tance, restricting their practical energy storage capabilities. To address 
this, heteroatom doping and composite formation with metal oxides 
have gained significant attention as strategies to introduce pseudoca -
pacitance, enhance conductivity, and improve electrochemical 
performance [ 8 , 13 – 15 ].

biodegradability, and rich functional groups ( – NH ₂ and – OH) that allow

chitosan-based composites for supercapacitor electrodes, demonstrating 
improved capacitance through doping and hybridization with conduc -

has shown excellent capacitive behavior across acidic, neutral, and

chitosan-derived electrodes [ 25 ]. Additionally, chitosan-based activated

ABSTRACT: The rapid demand for sustainable, high-performance energy
storage has accelerated the development of biomass-derived electrode materials
for next-generation supercapacitors. However, the intrinsically low electrical
conductivity and limited electrochemical activity of many metal oxide electrodes
remain major challenges that restrict their practical application. In this work, a
novel Fe-doped ZnO/activated carbon composite derived from oil palm empty
fruit bunches (Fe-ZnO/AC) was successfully synthesized via a hydrothermal
method and employed as an electrode material for asymmetric supercapacitors.
ZnO was selected for its low-cost, abundance, nontoxicity, and facile synthesis,
while Fe doping was introduced to enhance electrical conductivity, charge-
transfer kinetics, and redox activity. Simultaneously, activated carbon derived
from empty fruit bunch (EFB) waste provides a conductive, porous carbon
matrix that facilitates ion diffusion and electron transport. This study highlights
the synergistic integration of Fe-doped ZnO with activated carbon, enabling simultaneous enhancement of conductivity,
electrochemical performance, structural stability, and sustainability within a single-electrode system, a strategy that remains rarely
explored for asymmetric supercapacitor applications. The Fe-ZnO/AC electrode exhibited a high specific capacitance of 458.2 F g

−1

and 20.5 W h kg
−1
with power densities of 239.7 and 240.4 W kg
−1
, respectively. These findings demonstrate the excellent
electrochemical performance, stability, and energy storage capability of the Fe-ZnO/AC composite, highlighting its strong potential
as a low-cost, sustainable, and high-performance electrode material for next-generation asymmetric supercapacitors.

The global demand for high-performance, environmentally
friendly, and efficient energy storage systems continues to rise
in line with the rapid advancement of modern technologies.
Among various options, supercapacitors have attracted
significant attention due to their density, rapid charge−
discharge capability, and excellent cycling stability compared
to conventional batteries.
1−5
However, their relatively low
energy density remains a limitation.
6
Consequently, the
development of advanced electrode materials capable of
simultaneously delivering high capacitance and long-term
stability has become a research focus. In this context, transition
metal oxides and porous carbon materials are emerging as
promising candidates, as they offer complementary charge-
storage pseudocapacitance and electric double-layer capaci-
tance (EDLC) mechanisms, respectively.

mechanisms, EDLC and pseudocapacitance. In EDLC systems,
charge storage occurs through the electrostatic accumulation of
electrolyte ions at the electrode/electrolyte interface without
involving faradaic reactions, enabling excellent power capability
and long-term cycling stability.

attention as pseudocapacitive materials because of their
multiple oxidation states and rich redox activity. However,
their practical applications are often limited by poor electrical
conductivity and structural instability during repeated charge−
discharge cycles.
12

1. Introduction
Corn straw is the second most produced agricultural residue on a 
global scale. The annual yield of corn straw is 1,661,250 tonnes, rep -
resenting 27.2 % of the total agricultural waste [ 1 – 3 ]. Conventional 
methods of handling maize straw, such as incineration or haphazard 
piling, have been shown to result in a range of environmental issues. 
These include air pollution (e.g., PM2.5, CO
2
) and methane emissions, 
which can trigger eutrophication of water bodies and affect soil micro -
bial communities [ 4 , 5 ]. The carbonization of corn straw to produce 
capacitive carbon materials offers numerous advantages in terms of 
environmental sustainability. Its entire life cycle eco-efficiency is sub -
stantial, making it well-suited to the development of a carbon-neutral 
and circular economy [ 6 , 7 ]. Capacitive carbon materials have a long 
service life in supercapacitors, enabling carbon sequestration for a 
longer period compared to the natural decomposition of straw (1 – 2 
years to release carbon) [ 8 – 12 ].
Corn straw has a widely distributed vascular bundle. The secondary 
cell wall of straw consists of cellulose (which provides the backbone), 
hemicellulose (which connects the cellulose), and lignin (which fills the 
cross-links) to form a dense composite system. When the straw is used

wall hinders the diffusion of the activator, resulting in an uneven dis -

feedstock are employed to activate high-performance activated carbon 
materials using conventional process methods [ 15 , 16 ]. In this study, 
Fenton-like reagent pretreatment was employed to minimize the quan -
tity of activator during the fabrication of high-performance activated 
carbon materials.

Keywords: anode | biocoke | biographite | delayed coking | lithium-ion batteries | pyrolysis oil | sustainable aviation fuel
ABSTRACT
Catalytic graphitization of biomass-derived carbon offers a promising route to produce biographite as a sustainable alternative to
petroleum-based synthetic graphite for lithium-ion battery (LIB) anodes. This study investigates the physicochemical properties of
biocokes produced from pyrolysis oil at carbonization temperatures ranging from 150°C to 500°C. Using an iron (Fe) catalyst,
graphitization was performed at 1500°C, significantly lower than the /C243000°C required for conventional synthetic graphite. The
effects of introducing an intermediate-temperature hold (400°C –600°C) prior to graphitization were evaluated, simulating a
“delayed coking ” process to enable the coproduction of sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs). Chemical structure evolution during
biocoke formation was analyzed, and proposed mechanisms are presented. Biographites produced via the delayed coking pathway
exhibited high crystallinity and excellent electrochemical performance in both half-cell and full-cell LIB configurations. The full
cells exhibited an initial discharge capacity close to the theoretical capacity of the NMC622 cathode (175 mAh/g at 4.2 V), and high
capacity retention (/C2488%) after 150 cycles. Notably, the graphitic and electrochemical properties remained stable across the range
of intermediate hold temperatures. These findings provide a foundation for optimizing temperature parameters in delayed coking
systems to enable scalable, integrated production of biographite and SAFs from pyrolysis oil.
1 | Introduction
Rechargeable lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) were developed and
commercialized as high-performing and cost-effective energy stor-
age systems. Since commercialization in 1991, LIBs have revolu-
tionized the electrochemical energy storage technology owing to
their high energy density, light-weight nature, small size, high
Coulombic efficiency (CE), long cycle life, good rate performance,
high working voltage, minimal self-discharge, negligible memory
effect, etc [ 1–5]. The LIBs are extensively used in portable
electronic devices, grid energy storage, and electric vehicles
(EVs). The EVs, powered by LIBs, can achieve longer driving
ranges and are transforming the automotive sector by offering a

Uncontrolled bleeding under wet and deformable conditions remains a major challenge for conventional he -
mostatic materials, which often suffer from limited tissue adhesion and poor mechanical adaptability. Here, we 
developed an injectable sodium alginate hydrogel ionically cross-linked with Ca

⁺ and reinforced with hazelnut

containing hydrogel exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behavior, high injectability, enhanced wet tissue

shortened the clotting time to 4.4 min compared with 7.5 min for the untreated blood control and 7.2 min for 
Surgicel ® . In vivo evaluation in rat tail transection and liver injury models showed effective hemorrhage control, 
reducing blood loss by approximately 45 – 55% compared with untreated controls, while subcutaneous implan -
tation demonstrated acceptable biocompatibility without evidence of significant systemic toxicity or adverse 
histopathological responses. These findings demonstrate that HB reinforcement provides a simple and effective 
strategy for developing injectable alginate hydrogels with improved mechanical adaptability and localized he -
mostatic performance under wet and deformable conditions.

ABSTRACT
Water scarcity and salinity pose critical challenges that necessitate the development of efficient 
desalination processes for brackish water treatment. This study investigates the use of activated carbon 
derived from date palm pollen as a potential electrode material for batch capacitive deionization (CDI). 
Activated carbon exhibits an exceptionally large surface area of 2586.9 m²·g −1, as determined by 
Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, which provides numerous sites for electrostatic ion 
accumulation during CDI operation. When activated carbon is used as an electrode in batch CDI 
experiments with a 500 ppm NaCl feedstock at an applied cell voltage of 1.2 V, the electrode exhibits a 
salt adsorption capacity (SAC) of 38.0 mg·g−1 after 120 min of adsorption. These results indicate effective 
electrosorptive salt removal from brackish water under practical operating conditions. Additionally, 
electrochemical measurements reveal that the activated carbon electrodes exhibit a high specific 
capacitance of 92 F·g −1, indicating efficient storage of electric charge in electric double layers. The high 
SAC and specific capacitance and the large BET surface area confirm that the date-palm-pollen-derived 
activated carbon is a promising electrode material for batch CDI desalination systems.

ABSTRACT
Selective ion separation is essential for effective water treatment and resource recovery. Conventional techniques, such as 
adsorption, coagulation/flocculation, and membrane technologies, suffer from low selectivity, substantial cost, and high energy 
requirements. Alternatively, ion separation using capacitive deionization (CDI) has shown strong potential for energy efficiency, 
cost‐effectiveness, environmental sustainability, and selective removal. However, traditional carbon electrodes used in CDI have 
limitations for selective separations. MXene‐based electrodes present an attractive alternative for CDI due to their exceptional 
electrochemical properties. Nevertheless, MXenes are typically unstable over extended cycles, and to achieve ion selectivity, 
controlled interlayer spacing adjustment is required. Methods such as hybridization and functionalization can improve the 
selectivity properties of MXenes by tailoring their interlayer spacing. Several studies have reported the use of MXenes as CDI 
electrodes; however, most focus on brackish water desalination, while selective ion separation is rarely addressed. This review 
presents an in‐depth analysis of the role of modified MXene electrodes in advancing ion‐selective CDI technologies, exploring 
various strategies to achieve the desired selectivity. Moreover, it highlights critical challenges that hinder scalability and 
practical implementation. Finally, the review showcases the strategic roadmap for future opportunities toward next‐generation 
water purification and resource recovery solutions.

1. Introduction 
The global shift toward sustainable energy systems necessitates the development of advanced 
energy storage technologies capable of mitigating the intermittent nature of renewable energy 
sources such as solar and wind [1], [2] . Electrochemical capacitors (ECs), commonly known as 
supercapacitors, have gained significant attention as promising candidates in this transition due to 
their high-power density, fast charge–discharge rates, and excellent cycle stability [3]. Compared to 
conventional batteries, ECs offer superior operational safety and reliability; however, their relatively 
low energy density continues to constrain their widespread adoption in large -scale ap plications, 
including electric vehicles and grid-level energy storage systems. 
Article information  Abstract 
 
Article History 
Received 08 October 2025 
Revised   27 October 2025 
Accepted 18 November 2025 
Available online 02 December 2025 
 This work reports the development of an electrode material derived from 
bamboo stem via NaOH activation, integrating hierarchical porosity, and 
surface functionalization for electrochemical capacitor applications. The 
synthesized carbon exhibits a flaky, fibrous morphology with micro –
mesoporous networks as confirmed by SEM, and a predominantly 
amorphous structure with short -range graphitic ordering from XRD. 
Elemental analysis via EDS reveals a high ca rbon content (94.65%) and 
nitrogen content (3.4%), which enhances charge storage and electrical 
conductivity. BET and BJH analyses indicate a high surface area (865 –
1147 m²/g), a pore volume of 0.552 cm³/g, and an average pore diameter 
of 2.43 nm, favourab le for ion diffusion and electrolyte access. 
Electrochemical testing demonstrates a high specific capacitance of 833 
F/g at 0.5 A/g, attributed to combined electric double -layer capacitance 
and pseudocapacitive contributions from oxygen- and nitrogen-containing 
functional groups, as evidenced by FTIR and CV (b = 0.787; 21% 
diffusion-controlled contribution). Electrochemical impedance 
spectroscopy shows a low equivalent series resistance of 0.2 Ω, while 
charge–discharge cycling confirms excellent stability w ith 94% 
capacitance retention after 5000 cycles. The CV and GCD further confirm 
its potency for efficient charge transport and high energy storage 
performance. These findings highlight the potential of bamboo -derived 
activated carbon as a sustainable and c ost-effective electrode material. 
However, the overall energy and power densities remain constrained by 
the narrow voltage window of the aqueous electrolyte and the limited 
cycling evaluation, indicating the need for further study with other 
electrolytes with higher voltage window and long-term testing.

carbon, Porous structures

Novel hierarchical porous carbon materials derived from bamboo shoot shells

Fanen Zeng Yaning Zhang Qi Lv Hao Xie Bing Xu*

Abstract 
Porous carbon material s were synthesized from bamboo shoot shells through carbonization and static air 
activation.  The physicochemical properties of bamboo shoot shell -based porous carbon (BBC) were observed 
by scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, X -ray photoelectron spectroscopy, 
and N 2 adsorption desorption analysis. BBC has an optim al hierarchical porous structure that displays a 
specific surface area of 546.04 m 2 g-1 and an average pore diameter of 3.28 nm.  The formation mechanism 
of the BBC, which has a hierarchical porous structure in static air activation, was illustrated systematically. 
To evaluate the suitability of BBC for practical implementations further, the constructed symmetric 
supercapacitor achieved an energy density of 11.11 Wh kg -1 at a power density of 252 W kg -1 and an  
outstanding cyclic retention rate of 100% over 7,000 cycles at a current density of 10 A g -1. 
 
Keywords Supercapacitor Bamboo shoot shells  Hierarchical porous structure  Static air activation  
 
1 Introduction 
With the progress of society and the rapid growth of the economy, environmental pollution caused by the

ABSTRACT 
Biomass-derived porous carbons are promising electrodes for sustainable supercapacitors, but their performance depends on 
balancing charge-storage sites and ion-transport pathways. Herein, corn straw was converted into interconnected porous carbon 
through mild KHCO3 -assisted activation. The effects of activation temperature and holding time on pore architecture and 
capacitive behavior were comparatively evaluated, and the surface chemistry of the best-performing sample was further examined. 
CSK-750-2, prepared at 750◦C for 2 h, exhibited a hierarchical porous structure containing micropores and mesopores with a 
specific surface area of 1701 m2 g− 1 . Micropores provided abundant surface area for electric double-layer charge storage, whereas 
mesopores facilitated electrolyte-ion transport, and surface oxygen-containing groups may provide a limited Faradaic contribution. 
CSK-750-2 delivered 157 F g− 1 at 0.5 A g− 1 with 86% capacitance retention at 5 A g− 1 . The symmetric supercapacitor achieved 10.5 
Wh kg− 1 at 500 W kg− 1 and approximately 106% capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles. These results highlight the importance 
of balancing micropore-based charge storage and mesopore-assisted ion transport in biomass-derived carbon electrodes.

long cycling life, and operational safety [ 1–8 ]. Recent advances 
in graphene-based and flexible electrochemical energy-storage 
systems have further demonstrated the importance of elec- 
trode architecture, surface chemistry, and electrode–electrolyte 
interactions in determining energy-storage performance [ 9–11 ]. 
Carbon materials have been widely investigated as supercapac- 
itor electrodes because of their physicochemical stability, large 
specific surface area, favorable charge-transport characteristics, 
and tunable pore architecture [ 12–18 ]. In particular, biomass-

because of their renewable origin, abundant availability, low cost, 
environmental compatibility, and adjustable surface chemistry. 
Engineered biochar and biomass-derived carbon materials have 
also received increasing attention for sustainable energy and 
environmental applications [ 19 ].

widespread application of supercapacitors are low energy density
and narrow potential windows. Herein, the hybrid supercapacitor
with high energy density and wide potential window is constructed
via an in situ self-assembly method employing RGO-induced
flower-like MOF(Ni). Benefiting from the synergistic effect
between RGO and MOF(Ni), the interfacial interactions are
effectively improved, and the contact area with the electrolyte is
enhanced, which increases the ion transfer kinetics and overall

density of 70.16 Wh kg
−1
at a power density of 2200.09 W kg
−1
, outperforming most reported supercapacitors. This hybrid
supercapacitor exhibits excellent stability and high energy density, providing a novel strategy for further large-scale applications.

1. INTRODUCTION
Metal−organic frameworks (MOFs) represent a burgeoning
category of materials distinguished by metal clusters intricately
connected to organic ligands through coordinated bonds.
Remarkably, the meticulous choice of metal and organic
ligands during synthesis engenders the substantial latitude in
tailoring MOFs with diverse morphologies, sizes, and pore
architectures.
1−3
Consequently, MOFs hold significant poten-
tial for applications across various fields, including adsorption,
4

5

9,10
and energy storage.
11−13

structure, and inherent pseudocapacitive sites make them
exceptionally promising contenders for deployment as
electrode materials in supercapacitors. Currently, two primary
strategies are employed for MOFs in supercapacitor electrodes:
(1) direct utilization of MOFs to store electrical energy via the
electrochemical double-layer capacitor mechanism, leveraging
their inner surfaces;
14,15
(2) MOFs employed as sacrificial
templates or precursors, facilitating the transformation into
final materials (e.g., metal-based hydroxides, oxide, sulfides,
and porous carbon materials) by a straightforward annealing
method.
16−19

the challenges of insufficient conductivity, electrochemical
instability, and limited capacitance in MOFs persist as current
obstacles demanding resolution.

ABSTRACT: Black liquor is a typical wastewater and troublesome pollutant in the
papermaking industry, which is rich in lignin, hemicellulose, and residual alkali. Here,
we developed a short and e ﬃ cient process to prepare spherical hierarchical porous acti-
vated carbon from papermaking black liquor. The precursor was prepared by spray pyrol-
ysis of black liquor, where carbonization of black liquor, preliminary activation, and pore
formation are achieved under the synergistic e ﬀects of high temperature, water vapor, and
sodium/potassium hydroxides. The further activation was carried out using the residual
sodium and potassium compounds in the precursor material as etching agents.
Hierarchical porous amorphous carbon was achieved with the merits of ultrathin-walled
(10–20 nm) porous hollow spheres and a large amount of thin, bending, and reticular car-
bon nanosheets. Owing to its unique morphology, microstructure, and hierarchical pores,
the optimized sample AC700 presents a large speci ﬁc surface area of 2104.3 m
2 g–1 and a
pore volume of 1.139 cm 3 g–1. When evaluated as the cathode material of lithium-ion
capacitors, AC700 presents a high speci ﬁc capacity of 67.3 mAh g –1 within 2.0–4.0 V, along with excellent rate capability and cycling
stability. This work o ﬀers an e ﬃ cient and scalable pathway for high-value utilization of papermaking black liquor.

With the popularization of arti ﬁcial intelligence and battery-
driven electri ﬁcation, the demand for high-performance energy
storage devices is becoming increasingly urgent. 1–3 Lithium-
ion capacitors (LICs), characterized by high-power density,
excellent cycling stability, and relatively high energy density,
are considered promising candidates for applications requiring
rapid charge/discharge and long cycle life.
4,5 The performance
of LICs greatly depends on the properties of electrode mate-
rials.
6–8 Among various candidates, biomass-derived activated
carbon materials (orange peel, 2 coconut shells, 9 rice husks, 10,11
soybean straw, 12 wood,13 persimmon cores, 14 biowastes,6 etc.),
featuring high speci ﬁc surface area, hierarchical porosity, and
facile synthesis, are the most widely employed electrode mate-
rials for LICs
8,15 and supercapacitors,16 as well as catalyst carrier
materials.17,18
Lignin is a naturally occurring macromolecular polymer and
the second most abundant biopolymer in plants after cellulose,
making it one of the most abundant aromatic biomass resources
on Earth. Owing to its relatively high carbon content and favor-
able carbonization behavior, lignin has been widely regarded as
a promising precursor for the preparation of activated carbon
and other porous carbon materials.
19 For example, Nune
et al. 20 prepared porous carbon via lignin carbonization, which
exhibited a speci ﬁc surface area of 1092 m 2 g–1 and a capaci-
tance of 114 F g –1. Qiu et al. 21 synthesized a lignin-derived
mesoporous carbon cage by multi-stage explosion through ther-

2O4), achieving a
speciﬁc surface area of 1175.6 m 2 g–1. Wang et al. 22 prepared

ciﬁc surface area of 1998.4 m
2 g–1. Despite these advances,
the large-scale utilization of lignin remains challenging due to
its heterogeneous structure and the need for complicated
extraction processes.

Derived from Conocarpus and Lemon Tree Waste

ABSTRACT: Pesticide residues in aquatic systems pose persistent risks to
ecosystems and public health, underscoring the need for low-cost and
sustainable remediation strategies. In this study, biochars prepared from
Conocarpus branch waste (CBB) and lemon tree branch waste (LBB) via
slow pyrolysis at 450 °C were evaluated as adsorbents for two widely
applied agrochemicals: imidacloprid (IMI) and myclobutanil (MYC).
Comprehensive physicochemical characterization (SEM, TEM, BET, and
elemental analysis) revealed mesoporous structures with distinct surface
features. Batch adsorption experiments demonstrated strong dependence
on solution pH, adsorbent dosage, contact time, and initial pesticide
concentration. Under near-neutral conditions (pH 7.0, 5 g L
−1
, 25 °C, 24
h), maximum capacities reached 8.69 mg g
−1
(IMI) and 12.31 mg g
−1
(MYC) for CBB. Adsorption kinetics followed a pseudo-second-order
model (R
2
> 0.98), while equilibrium data fit both Langmuir and the Freundlich isotherms (R
2
≥ 0.99). Thermodynamic analyses
(ΔG° = −1.3 to −4.5 kJ mol
−1
; ΔH° = −16.4 to −29.8 kJ mol
−1
) indicated spontaneous, exothermic processes dominated by
physisorption. The reusability of both biochars across multiple cycles further confirmed their practical applicability. These results
highlight pruning-waste biochars as effective and sustainable alternatives to conventional adsorbents for mitigating pesticide
pollution in water.
1. INTRODUCTION
Pesticides play a vital role in modern agriculture, serving as
essential tools for controlling pests and diseases while
significantly enhancing crop yields and ensuring food security.
1
With the continuous growth of the global population, the
demand for food production is expected to increase,
necessitating a greater reliance on pesticides to sustain
agricultural output.
2
However, despite their advantages, the
widespread use of these products has raised serious environ-
mental and health concerns. As pesticides are extensively
applied, their residues and degradation byproducts can
infiltrate aquatic ecosystems through spray drift, surface runoff,
and leaching, posing substantial threats to water quality,
biodiversity, and human health.
3,4
Furthermore, contamination of groundwater and aquifers
exacerbates these concerns, creating long-term environmental
and public health challenges.
5,6
Among the widely used
pesticides, imidacloprid (1-[(6-chloro-3-pyridyl)methyl]-N-
nitroimidazolidin-2-ylideneamine) (Figure 1a), a neonicoti-
noid insecticide synthesized in 1985, has become one of the
most prevalent insecticides globally.
7,8
Its application spans soil
treatment, seed coating, and foliar spraying.
9−11
However,
imidacloprid exhibits high water solubility, increasing its
potential for leaching into surface and groundwater systems.
12
Its environmental persistence has resulted in frequent
detections in water bodies worldwide.
13
Myclobutanil (2-(4-
chlorophenyl)-2-(1H-1,2,4-triazol-1-ylmethyl)-hexanenitrile)
(Figure 1b), a broad-spectrum systemic fungicide from the
azole class, is widely used in agriculture to combat fungal
pathogens,
